items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I saw people there that I, you know, had heard about, read about, you know. You couldn't say you had seen them because you didn't see them unless you saw them in the movies... There were some real famous persons.

ctx.x: Dunbar Hotel, and at the club. At that time the Club Alabam. I don't know how I got into the Club Alabam. I didn't talk about that, oh my gracious me, well that was something. The thing that was so exciting, Pat, when I first came here, was the fact that everybody, anybody who was anybody went to Central Avenue, you see. This Club Alabam was the living end. It was just something else, really. I saw people there that I, you know, had heard about, read about, you know. You couldn't say you had seen them because you…

Eddie Anderson, who later became Rochester, was working there with a partner, and this partner's name was Johnnie -- Johnnie, Johnnie, Johnnie, I can't think of it. Johnnie Taylor, his partner's name was Johnnie Taylor, and they had the most -- honestly, this was the funniest, the most comical act, together. They used to do acts with mops and brooms, you know. They'd be mopping the floor and going on, and all of a sudden they'd stop and tell jokes or something, and wisecracking at each other, you know. And…

Rochester was too. But this is the calibre of talent that was around. And my friend Lillian Randolph, who is still around today and doing very well. She has been in, oh God, so many marvelous pictures. She really went from the nightclub scene into the movies, you know, and to television, when television became -- in fact she was into radio first, because she did the Gildersleeve, and she was on Amos and Andy, and incidentally, the woman that was her sister, that was the mother on Amos and Andy, who was Amanda…
